A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same E-NES research work, with 34 complete pages including Appendices A-F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish only a localized correction in Section 4.2, accompanying spacing changes, and an updated arXiv stamp.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original OpenFWI and spherical travel-time experiments, scalability results, ablations, and qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: V3 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix E, including benchmark comparisons, scalability studies, and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 restores the description of the existing encoder E. Its cross-attention computations, projection head, losses, and training and inference procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten 2D OpenFWI categories, extruded 3D Style-B data, spherical velocity fields, and path-planning and steerability scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator participation is unchanged: FC-DeepONet in Table 1, Functa in Table 2, FMM in Figure 3, and the same variants in the ablations.

E3.justification: Data splits, source grids, evaluation metrics, training and fitting budgets, and model configurations are identical, including the settings in Appendices C-E.

E4.justification: The equivariance, pretraining, embedding, latent-design, fitting-epoch, qualitative, and empirical steerability analyses are retained unchanged in Figure 2 and Appendix E.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is identical. No run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-6 and all result plots and visualizations are unchanged. Table 1 still shows converged autodecoding outperforming FC-DeepONet on seven of ten datasets.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, propositions, theorems, derivations, and appendix proofs are unchanged. The restored encoder signature in Section 4.2 summarizes the existing mapping rather than introducing new mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and Section 6 retain the same claims about equivariant travel-time prediction, grid-free operation, generality, scalability, and empirical performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of geometric conditioning, accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs, comparative limitations, and broader applicability in Section 6 and Appendices E-F are identical.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, data-processing descriptions, and code-access information are unchanged. The repaired encoder introduction adds no implementation information beyond the existing architecture description.

R1.justification: The cited works are identical. The restored attribution to Wessels et al. in Section 4.2 restates the extension relationship already described in Section 4.1.

P1.justification: V3 repairs the broken opening sentence of Section 4.2 by introducing E: M × M × P(Z) → R^L as an extension of Wessels et al.'s invariant cross-attention encoder. The only other textual change is the arXiv version/date stamp.

P2.justification: The repaired paragraph occupies an additional line and slightly redistributes vertical spacing on page 6. All figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 replaces a visibly incomplete architecture sentence with a clear introduction to the encoder and its relationship to prior work. This provides a limited clarity improvement; the scientific content, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
